entries.example: A seed wakes up and sprouts: the seed rests in the soil, and with water, warmth and light it wakes up, growing a root down and a green shoot up into a seedling.
entries.meaning: The start of a plant's life: it rests in the soil and wakes up with water, warmth and light, then sprouts a root and a shoot.

entries.example: In scenes s1 and s2, follow one seed as a worked example: the seed wakes up in the soil and sprouts, so one seed becomes a seedling; the seedling grows into an adult plant with a flower, and inside that flower new seeds form. Each step is a change of state, and the new seeds can start the whole cycle again.
entries.meaning: The baby plant that has just sprouted from a seed: it grows taller and stronger until it becomes an adult plant.

entries.example: Watch out: the flower is not the end of the plant: the seedling grows into an adult plant with a flower, and inside the flower new seeds are forming, ready to start the cycle again.
entries.meaning: The showy part of the adult plant: new seeds form inside it, so it starts the next round of the cycle instead of ending it.

entries.example: An egg hatches into a caterpillar: a butterfly lays tiny eggs on a leaf, and each egg hatches into a caterpillar that munches leaves and grows bigger.
entries.meaning: The growing-up stage of a butterfly: it hatches from an egg and munches leaves to grow bigger.

entries.example: The butterfly emerges and the cycle repeats: the caterpillar rests inside a pupa while its body changes, then an adult butterfly emerges and lays eggs, so the cycle repeats.
entries.meaning: The resting case a caterpillar forms: inside it, the caterpillar's body changes into a butterfly.

entries.example: Name the stages of a butterfly life cycle: egg, caterpillar, pupa, adult butterfly
entries.meaning: The circle of changes a living thing goes through as it grows: the adult makes new young, and the circle starts again.
